page: Amazon Web Services m6i.large is a general-purpose virtual server built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing dedicated CPU allocation. It includes 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance for single-core operations, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1880.69 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1537.0. However, multi-core and memory scaling are limited. The stress-ng multi-core score is 1922.88, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 1710.0, both falling into the lower performance percentiles. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read-only and write speeds measuring 14.73 GB/sec and 13.18 GB/sec respectively. Cryptographic and compression tasks perform moderately, with single-threaded gzip compression reaching 27.96 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m6i.large serves as an entry-level general-purpose resource. It provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio suitable for workloads that do not require high parallel processing power or massive memory throughput. Given the single physical core configuration and weak multi-core scaling, this instance is best fit for light web serving, basic text processing, single-threaded applications, and small-scale development or testing environments.
